lines.meet: G'day, I'm Callum, I'll be up front taking the bites. Don't mind the scorpion on my shoulder, mate, she's a softie once you get to know her.
lines.meet_neighbour: You're down in the Southern Barrens too, aren't you? I'm Callum, from the hut full of jars. Pop in any time, the jars mostly stay shut.
lines.ask_home: Whereabouts are you from, mate? I can never pick accents, and I've stopped trying.
lines.ask_work: What'd you do for a crust, back home? I reckon everyone's got a good story in there somewhere.
lines.answer_home: Brisbane, mate, hot and sticky and full of things that'll bite you, which is probably why I turned out like this.
lines.answer_work: Sixteen years at a reptile sanctuary. Taipans, death adders, crocs, and school groups who all asked the same question about the same snake.
lines.chat_food: I'd kill for a meat pie with sauce from a servo at two in the morning. It's terrible food and I'd eat three.
lines.chat_sleep: I sleep like a log, mate, always have. A snake house at night is the most peaceful place in the world, believe it or not.
lines.chat_missing: Feeding time at the snake house, warm and quiet, everything settling down for the night. Best hour of the day, that was.
lines.chat_here: Everything here's got venom or teeth, and half the people want to kill it on sight. Most of it's just scared, mate, same as back home.
lines.tease_quiet: {name}, you're quieter than a carpet python in winter. I've had to check you're breathing twice today.
lines.tease_talker: {name}, mate, you'd talk the leg off a chair. I reckon the chair would thank you for it, mind.
lines.tease_careful: {name}, you look at every rock like there's a death adder under it. Fair enough, there usually is, but still.
lines.tease_bold: {name}, you've got the survival instincts of a kid at a reptile show. I mean that with love, mate.
lines.tease_any: {name}, you're like a good blue-tongue lizard. Ugly at first, then you grow on people.
lines.tease_back: Ha, too right, {name}, I walked into that one. Fair cop, mate.
lines.take_it_kindly: No worries, {name}, I've been called worse by a croc. Well, he didn't call me anything, but he meant it.
lines.bristle: Nah, leave that one, {name}. That's not one for joking about, mate.
lines.apologise: Sorry, mate, that came out rough. I'm better with snakes than people, as you can probably tell.
lines.double_down: Nah, I meant it, mate. I'd say it to your face and I just did.
lines.needle_quiet: Mate, how am I meant to know what's going on in there? Even a goanna hisses first.
lines.needle_talker: Mate, you've got to stop talking. You're scaring off everything for miles, and some of it I wanted to meet.
lines.needle_careful: You poke everything with a stick before you go near it, and it's driving me spare. Animals hate that, and so do I.
lines.needle_bold: You charge at everything, mate, and then it bites you and you're surprised. Of course it bit you.
lines.needle_any: You keep treating everything out here like it's evil. It's not, mate, it's frightened, and you're enormous.
lines.bite_back: Mate, I've been bitten by things that'd kill you in an hour. Don't tell me how to handle myself.
lines.hurt: Fair enough, mate, that one got under the scales. I'll go and have a word with my scorpion.
lines.laugh_off: Ha, you'll have to do better than that, mate. My sister's a lawyer, she's been having a go at me for forty years.
lines.confide: {name}, I had to leave my dog behind when all this happened. I miss her more than I miss most people, and I know how that sounds.
lines.listen: Thanks for telling me, {name}. No rush, mate, I'm not going anywhere.
lines.look_out: {name}, let me go in first on this one. I'm built for getting bitten, and you're not.
lines.accept: No worries, {name}. I'll do what you say, mate.
lines.deflect: She'll be right, {name}. I've had worse from a cranky python.
lines.check_in: {name}, you right, mate? Show me where it got you, I know a bit about bites.
lines.blame: Somebody went poking where they shouldn't have, and we all paid for it. I'm not saying who, mate, but you know.
lines.thank: Mate, you dragged me back from somewhere I didn't like the look of. Thanks, I owe you a beer.
lines.brush_off: No worries at all, mate. Sit still for a bit and drink some water.
lines.worry: {name}, that one scared me, mate. Sit down a minute before you do anything else.
lines.handed_down: Mate, this one was yours, wasn't it? I'll keep it in one piece for you.
lines.hand_fine: Nah, you keep it, mate. Suits you better, and I've got my scorpion.
lines.hand_sulk: Bit rough, that. Nobody asked me, mate.
lines.turn_friendly: {name}, you're good value, mate. Reckon you'd be all right with a snake on your arm.
lines.turn_friends: {name}, you're my mate now, properly. I'd let you meet Biscuit if she were here, and that's the highest honour I've got.
lines.turn_grating: We don't really get on, do we, mate? No worries, we'll stay out of each other's way.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll still take the bites in front of you, mate, because that's the job. Don't expect a beer after.
lines.make_up: Reckon we start over, {name}? I've been a bit of a goose with you, mate.
lines.defend: Oi, leave {name} alone, mate. That wasn't anybody's fault and you know it.
lines.friend_left: {name}'s headed home for a bit. It's not the same without them, mate, I'll be honest with you.
lines.friend_back: Good to have you back, {name}! I was running out of people to tell about snakes.
lines.common_venom: I've spent my whole life around things with venom in them, mate, and I've been bitten by most of them. You've done the same, I reckon.
lines.common_aussie: You're an Aussie too? Mate, where from? I haven't heard a proper accent in years.
lines.common_animals: I've always been better with animals than people, mate. Give me a frightened snake over a crowd any day.
